correctness.rationale: Any nonempty cross-bifix-free family has one common endpoint orientation because all first/last bits differ and mixed orientations cause length-one conflict. Reversing if needed, every word has interior ones i<j and a final one. If a=min i and b=min j over the family, overlap constraints imply a+b>n: if not, prefix 0^(a-1)1 of a witness equals suffix of another ending at its second interior one. Conversely when a+b>n, every prefix ending at its first/second interior one has fewer 1s than the corresponding suffix (1 versus ≥2, or 2 versus 3); prefixes ending in zero cannot match a suffix ending in one. Every valid family is contained in the threshold family F_{n,a}, whose size (a-1)(2n-3a)/2 is a concave quadratic, giving exact maximum and forcing equality with full F. Integer vertex a=n/3+1/2 gives ties only when n=3m and the stated four (else two) labeled optima after reversal. Independent exhaustive oriented subset enumeration at n=4..8 returned sizes 1,2,3,5,7 and oriented maximizer counts 1,1,2,1,1.
